title: Elastic envelopes: capacity escrow and deferred burst PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an "elastic envelopes" feature that lets tenants deposit capacity credits into an escrow-like reservoir that can be consumed for deferred burst capacity. The feature combines an API and console UX for managing envelopes, a routing/handshake protocol to honor escrow credits across scheduler boundaries, and operator controls for reconciliation and emergency reclaim. Purpose: reduce noisy neighbor impact while enabling predictable transient burst behavior for reserved tenants.
goals: Allow tenants to create one or more elastic envelopes (time-limited or credit-limited) tied to their dedicated reservation
Enable controlled deferred bursts: consumption from envelope does not count against baseline reservation until a reconciliation window elapses
Surface envelope balances, usage history, and forecast in Console; provide programmatic API to top-up and withdraw
Provide guardrails so envelope usage cannot silently exceed SLO budgets for other tenants (preemption / fallback policies)
Ship initial operator reconciliation tooling and audit logs for financial/billing reconciliation
non_goals: Not a replacement for global autoscaling or long-term overcommit policies
Will not change core scheduling algorithms beyond a lightweight handshake and priority flagging
Does not implement multi-cloud cross-region credit transfer in v1
requirements: API: POST/GET/PUT/DELETE endpoints for envelopes with fields: tenant_id, envelope_id, credit_units, ttl_seconds, policy (preemptible|non-preemptible), tags
Console: New ‘Envelopes’ tab under Dedicated -> Reservations listing active envelopes with balance and last-activity; top-up modal and one-click withdraw

Scheduler/Router: On request, if reservation exhausted, consult envelope balance via cached ledger; if envelope policy=non-preemptible allow immediate route to reserved pool else route to fallback model variant
Reconciliation: Periodic ledger that marks consumed credits and emits audit entries; operator UI to reconcile disputes
Telemetry: Emit metrics per-tenant: envelope_balance, envelope_consumed_rate, envelope_preemptions, envelope_reconcile_failures
Billing: Expose envelope transactions to billing export with invoice-line references
Safety: A global circuit breaker for envelope consumption per-subnet and per-zone to prevent noisy neighbor storms
Auth/ZK: Envelope operations are RBAC-protected; only tenant admins and Redwood operators can reconcile/force-withdraw
acceptance_criteria: API acceptance: Create/read/update/delete operations succeed; validation rejects negative credits; TTL respected (expired envelopes marked and prevented from being used)
Console acceptance: Envelopes tab lists created envelopes within 5s of creation; top-up operation updates balance within 10s and shows history; UI passes accessibility checklists
Routing acceptance: Synthetic canary shows that a deferred-burst request consumes envelope credits and p95 latency for reserved requests under burst remains < 1.5x baseline when envelope used
Fallback acceptance: When envelope depleted, requests are routed to configured fallback variant (cheaper quantized model) without request loss; no silent failures
Reconciliation acceptance: Operator can run a manual reconcile for a tenant and reconcile report matches ledger export within 0.01% discrepancy over a 24h window
Telemetry acceptance: Metrics are visible in Console and exported to internal monitoring with tags tenant_id and envelope_id
Billing acceptance: Billing export includes envelope transactions in the next invoice cycle and there is a test invoice for a sandbox tenant
Security acceptance: Envelope actions require tenant-admin role; operator reconcile actions are logged to audit trail and reviewed in security sign-off
success_metrics: Less than 5% of dedicated tenants need emergency revoke due to envelope misuse in first 90 days
Average time-to-top-up via Console < 15s for 90% of customers
Fallback routing prevents SLA violations for >95% of burst events that exceed reservations
Operator reconcile disputes < 2 per 10k envelope-transactions after first month
rollout_plan: Week 1–2: Engineering spike and prototyping of ledger and API; UX sketches and internal feedback
Week 3: Implement API and minimal ledger + unit tests; basic Console list view behind feature flag
Week 4: Scheduler handshake integration and canary with sandbox tenants; add telemetry and billing hooks
Week 5: Internal beta with 3 pilot customers (contracted); operator reconcile UI and runbook
Week 6: Security review, load testing, and performance tuning; start slow ramp in production (10% of tenants) with monitor alerts
Week 7: Full rollout and deprecate experimental flags; post-launch evaluation after 30 days
open_decisions: Envelope unit definition: Should credits be tokenized per-inference-second or normalized to vCPU-equivalent? (engineering prefers normalized unit)
Preemption semantics: Whether non-preemptible envelopes should still be allowed to be forcibly reclaimed under emergency operator action
Default TTL: sensible default 24h vs 7d for envelopes created via Console
